# `supabase/rls-no-policies`: Row Level Security enabled but no policies

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family   | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| supabase | low              | 2.5                      | [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-1188](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1188.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Tables in exposed schemas that have RLS enabled but no permissive policy after all
migrations. The Data API then returns no rows and rejects every write for `anon` and
`authenticated`. Severity is **low**: the table is safe, but this state is rarely intended,
and the usual "fixes" are dangerous.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

With RLS on and no permissive policy, the API returns no rows and rejects every write for anon and authenticated users. That is safe, but it is rarely intended, and the usual "fixes" are dangerous: disabling RLS, adding USING (true), or calling the database with the service_role key from the browser. Tables meant to be server-only should say so explicitly.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- Table {table} has Row Level Security enabled but no permissive policies: the Data API denies all access to it.

## How to fix

Add the policies the app needs, scoped to the row owner. If only your server (service_role) should touch the table, make that explicit by revoking API privileges. VibeGuard then treats it as intentional.

### Vulnerable

```sql
alter table public.notes enable row level security;
-- no policies: the app breaks, and the next "fix" is often: disable row level security
```

### Fixed

```sql
-- Option A: user-owned rows
create policy "Owners manage their notes" on public.notes
  for all to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = owner)
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = owner);

-- Option B: server-only table, deliberately unreachable from the Data API
revoke all on public.stripe_events from anon, authenticated;
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Server-only tables** accessed only with the service-role key (queues, audit logs) are
  a legitimate use of "RLS on, no policies". Make it explicit with
  `REVOKE ALL ON … FROM anon, authenticated` (VibeGuard then treats the table as private),
  or suppress with the reason.
- **Restrictive-only policies** (`AS RESTRICTIVE`) do not grant access on their own, so a
  table with only restrictive policies is still reported.
- **Limitations:** policies created in the dashboard or by `DO` blocks are invisible
  (see [`supabase/rls-disabled`](rls-disabled.md)).

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```sql
-- vibeguard-ignore-next-line supabase/rls-no-policies -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the statement VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  supabase/rls-no-policies: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html): Improper Access Control
- [CWE-1188](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1188.html): Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default
